facts.raw_span: a right breast mass noted for more than 1 year
recently associated with skin ulceration
the mass had gradually enlarged, was hard in texture, non-tender, and mobile
a 3-cm area of skin breakdown with mild exudation and bleeding over the lesion
a 4.5 × 5.5 cm irregular, poorly defined, hard mass was palpable at the 1 o’clock position in the right breast
overlying ulceration and slight serosanguinous discharge
the lesion was fairly mobile without palpable axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
the left breast was normal
Breast ultrasound and MRI both classified the lesion as BI-RADS category V
Chest CT demonstrated a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy
Serum breast tumor markers were within normal limits

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a hard, mobile mass and overlying skin ulceration, combined with imaging findings of a BI-RADS category V lesion and a chest CT suggestive of malignancy, supports a diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma.
The patient's symptoms of skin ulceration, exudation, and bleeding over the lesion, as well as the presence of a hard, mobile mass, are consistent with inflammatory breast cancer.
The patient's presentation with skin ulceration and serosanguinous discharge, combined with a underlying breast mass, could be consistent with Paget's disease of the breast.
The patient's imaging findings and lack of serum tumor markers suggest a diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer, although further testing would be needed to confirm.

The patient's presentation with a hard, mobile mass and imaging findings suggestive of malignancy could be consistent with metaplastic breast cancer, although further testing would be needed to confirm.

rationales.F12: The description of the breast mass as suggestive of malignancy on imaging supports invasive ductal carcinoma.
